# correspond

A channel facade for AI agents: read, listen, write and identify the sender over GitHub, email, push notifications, Telegram and a web inbox, through one model and one set of verbs.

```bash
pip install correspond

correspond read github:octocat/hello-world#1        # an issue and its comments, through your gh login
correspond send ntfy: "backup finished" --dry-run    # the plan; nothing is contacted
correspond capabilities telegram                     # what a channel can do, graded
correspond requirements email                        # what it needs, and where to get it
```

Every channel gets the same shape. A **reference** names a conversation: `<channel>:<id>`. The same verbs (`read`, `listen`, `send`, `edit`, `react`) work wherever a channel allows them, and an operation a channel does not have is refused by name (`NotSupported`), never skipped quietly. Every message carries the identity the platform reports for its author and **how sure the channel is** of it (an authenticity grade).

correspond knows no people. Linking `github:someone` to a person is a people registry’s job, for example [acquaint](https://github.com/thorwhalen/acquaint).

## Channels

| Channel    | References                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Operations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Built on                                                                                                                                                                              |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `github`   | `github:owner/repo`, `github:owner/repo#12`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | read, listen (issues, comments, pull request review threads, discussions), send (opening an issue takes `native` labels, assignees, milestone; `native` category opens a discussion instead), edit, react, label, unlabel, close, reopen, verify (webhooks), audience                  | the `gh` CLI and its login; correspond holds no token                                                                                                                                 |
| `email`    | `email:` (the folder), `email:someone@example.org`; either takes `?folder=<name>` (a Gmail label is a folder), and `email:` takes `?from=<address or domain>,...` (a domain as `@example.org`); on Gmail, `?gmail=<search>` adds Gmail’s search syntax; quote such a reference in a shell: `'email:?folder=News'` | read, listen, send (with cc and bcc), upload (an attachment), audience                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `imaplib`, `smtplib`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ntfy`     | `ntfy:` (the default topic), `ntfy:<topic>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | send, audience                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `urllib`                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `macos`    | `macos:`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | send, audience                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `terminal-notifier` or `osascript`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `telegram` | `telegram:`, `telegram:<chat id>`, `telegram:@name`, `telegram:<chat id>/<topic id>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | listen (`getUpdates`, or a webhook on a server), read (what listening logged), send, edit, react, upload (a photo or a document), audience, verify (webhook deliveries)                                                                                                                | the Bot API over `urllib`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `signal`   | `signal:`, `signal:+<number>`, `signal:group.<id>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | listen (the REST API’s WebSocket, plus safety-number changes as `identity.changed`), read (what listening and sending logged: no history before linking), send, reply, audience                                                                                                        | `signal-cli-rest-api` over `urllib`; `websocket-client` to listen                                                                                                                     |
| `webinbox` | `webinbox:<site>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | read, listen, audience                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | the ASGI collector below, and `dol` stores                                                                                                                                            |
| `apprise`  | `apprise:<alias>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | send, audience                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | the `apprise` package, about 155 services (`pip install "correspond[apprise]"`)                                                                                                       |
| `gdrive`   | `gdrive:<folder id>` (or the folder’s URL)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | read (one message per file, the file attached, fetched on demand), audience (the folder’s sharing); read only                                                                                                                                                                          | pydrivedol and a service-account key, read-only scope (`pip install "correspond[gdrive]"`)                                                                                            |
| `discord`  | `discord:<channel id>` (a channel or a thread)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | read, listen (polling a channel over REST: new messages; or, with `DISCORD_LISTEN_VIA=gateway`, a resumed gateway window: new, edited and deleted messages), send (with replies; only user mentions ping), audience, verify (an HTTP interaction’s Ed25519 signature, graded `crypto`) | discorddol and a bot token (`pip install "correspond[discord]"`); the Message Content intent, or the bot reads empty text; `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY` for verify                            |
| `slack`    | `slack:<channel>` (a channel’s name, `#` optional, or its id); `slack:<channel>/<thread ts>` for one thread                                                                                                                                                                                                       | with a token: read, listen (polling, or pushed through the Events API receiver or Socket Mode), send (replies in threads), verify (signed requests); with only a webhook: send; with nothing: a dry run that renders the draft as Slack mrkdwn, ready to paste; audience               | `urllib`; `websocket-client` for Socket Mode (extra `slack`); `CORRESPOND_SLACK_TOKEN` (an app installed in your workspace), or a webhook URL in `CORRESPOND_SLACK_WEBHOOK_<CHANNEL>` |

Every v0.1 adapter uses the Python standard library. Apprise, Google Drive and Discord are extras, and each registers only when its extra is installed. Signal (through `signal-cli-rest-api`; its WebSocket client is the `signal` extra) is built too.

**Apprise** reaches the long tail (Discord and Slack webhooks, Matrix, Pushover, Gotify, SMS gateways…) for sending only. A reference names an *alias*, never an Apprise URL, because the URL carries the service’s credentials. An alias is 1-64 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` (case folded; `all` and `always` are Apprise’s match-everything tags and are refused). `apprise:<alias>` sends to the one URL in `CORRESPOND_APPRISE_URL_<ALIAS>` (upper case, `-` as `_`), else the Keychain item `correspond-apprise-url-<alias>`, else every URL tagged exactly `<alias>` in the local Apprise config file named by `config` under `[apprise]` (or `$CORRESPOND_APPRISE_CONFIG`); URLs tagged `always` are not added, so a mistyped alias reaches nobody. Apprise’s own logging, which prints URLs, is silenced while correspond calls it. A plan names the service (the URL’s scheme), never the URL. A partial delivery is `unconfirmed`, never retried blindly. A draft’s priority is not sent (Apprise services take one in their URL, if at all).

`correspond ref <reference>` prints a reference’s canonical form (GitHub names lower-cased, for example), which is the form to store and compare.

## Authenticity

| Grade      | Means                                                                                                                |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `platform` | the platform authenticated the account (GitHub, Telegram)                                                            |
| `crypto`   | a signed delivery checked with its secret (a GitHub webhook’s `X-Hub-Signature-256`)                                 |
| `bound`    | the host application signed an assertion about its logged-in user (the web inbox)                                    |
| `domain`   | email whose topmost `Authentication-Results`, added by a server you trust, records DMARC passing for the From domain |
| `claimed`  | nothing verified: a typed name, an ordinary From header, an anonymous report                                         |
| `forged`   | verification was attempted and failed                                                                                |

Grades are a vocabulary, not a ranking. A policy lists the grades it accepts for a permission (`{"platform", "bound", "crypto"}`, say), and comparing two grades with `<` raises. Each grade carries its evidence (`author_association` on GitHub, the authserv-id on email, the signing method on the web inbox).

## Capabilities

`correspond capabilities github` grades each operation `full`, `partial` or `none`, plus whether a write can start a conversation (`initiate`; a Telegram bot cannot), answer a specific message (`reply`), carry a `priority` or copy further recipients (`cc`), how far back `read` sees (`history_depth`), the limits (text length, reactions), the fields its messages carry in `native` (`native_fields`), the rate limits and notes. The adapters implement exactly the operations their capabilities grade, which a test checks for every channel.

```text
$ correspond react ntfy:example-topic m1 eyes
ntfy does not support react
```

## Who can read it

```text
$ correspond audience github:example/app#12
world-readable; emailed to watchers and participants; archived by others; edits keep a visible history; not retractable
scope: public
...
```

`correspond audience <reference>` says who can read a conversation, now and plausibly later, before anything is written to it. The first line is the answer in words; the rest is the record (`--json` prints it under `audience`, beside `hash` and `words`): a `scope` (`operator`, `named`, `group`, `org`, `public`), the `readers` known to read it with whether that list is `complete`, the reader `classes` that cannot be listed, whether `external` readers exist, what a send leaves behind (`durability`), how the readership can grow (`widening`), the `evidence` behind each value, and a `hash` that changes when the audience does (and only then, not with the time or the evidence).

**Unknown resolves to public.** A failed or forbidden lookup, a channel without an audience reader and a planned channel all answer `public` with `defaulted: true` and the reason in `evidence`. Nothing is cached: ask again right before sending. `correspond capabilities <channel>` grades how much each reader can tell.

| Channel                    | How the audience is computed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `github` (full)            | The repository’s visibility; its collaborators, when the `gh` account may list them; the organisation’s base permission, when the account may read it (otherwise the documented default, read). Never `complete`: installed apps, webhooks and an organisation’s security managers read without being listable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `email` (full)             | Scope `named`: the address plus `--cc` and `--bcc`, never `complete` (any address may be an alias, a shared mailbox or an auto-forward). A recipient outside the config’s `own_domains` makes it `external`. A list-shaped address (under `lists` in the config, or a local part such as `list`, `all`, `team`, `dev`, `announce`, `info`) adds a class for its unlistable members and `list_expansion`, and leaves `external` unknown when every address is internal. A Bcc address is a class of its own. Always `forwarding`, never retractable. |
| `telegram` (partial)       | `getChat`. A private chat is `named`, its reader identified by account id. A chat with a public username is `public`. A group, or a channel without a username, is `group`, and members are never listed. A linked discussion group or channel is read too, and makes the audience public when it is. New members read the history unless the chat hides it; forwards widen it unless its content is protected. A chat `getChat` cannot read is public, defaulted.                                                                                  |
| `signal` (partial)         | A person’s conversation is `named`. A group’s members come from the REST API (`complete` unless the group has an invite link, which makes it `public`). A lookup that fails is public, defaulted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ntfy` (partial)           | `public`, with the classes “anyone who knows the topic name” and whoever runs the server, unless the config says `denies_anonymous_read`. The cache window is a class; its length is evidence. Nothing is asked of the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `macos`, `webinbox` (full) | `operator`, retractable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `apprise` (partial)        | `public`, never `complete`: the service behind an alias can be one phone or a public channel, and nothing is asked of it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Writing: dry run first

- `--dry-run` on `send`, `edit` and `react` sends nothing and changes nothing. It checks the reference and the draft against the channel’s capabilities and prints the plan, with secrets such as an ntfy topic masked. A dry run reads only the environment and the config file, plus the audience lookup (a `gh api` call for GitHub, `getChat` with the bot token for Telegram): a value kept in the Keychain or on a remote host is otherwise looked up when sending, and the plan says so.
- `--cc` and `--bcc` (comma-separated) copy further recipients on channels that grade `cc` (email); elsewhere they are refused by name. Bcc addresses go on the envelope only, never in a header, and they count in the audience.
- `--notify` (comma-separated, `notify=` in Python) names who must be notified, and the writer guarantees it: on GitHub (and Telegram, for a member of the chat with a public username) a mention (`@octocat`) the text lacks is added on a closing `cc` line; on email an address that is neither To nor Cc goes in Cc, and so counts in the audience. The plan shows what was added (`mentions_added`, `cc_added`). A channel that cannot guarantee it refuses the draft with `NotSupported("notify")` rather than sending without it.
- **Files.** `correspond upload <ref> <path>` sends one file; `correspond send <ref> "text" --attach a.pdf,b.csv` sends files with the text (email: each attached; Telegram: one, the text its caption). Paths are read only when they are regular files outside hidden folders (`--include-hidden` to allow one), and the plan names each file’s real path. `--idempotency-key` keeps a retried upload from posting twice, and on Telegram `--native '{"as_document": true}'` sends an image as the file it is.
- **Every write (`send`, `edit`, `react`, `upload`, `label`, `unlabel`, `close`, `reopen`) passes the `before_send` check first** (an upload’s check sees only the file name), on the dry run too. The plan shows `audience` (who can read it, in words), `audience_hash`, and `before_send` (the verdict). With nothing configured the check lets the write go ahead, so the audience line is all it adds. A check can stop the write: `refused` (not as written, not here) or `needs_approval` (wait for the operator), with any details it attached in `before_send_details`. A configured check that does not load stops every write (`before_send_unavailable`), and one that crashes stops that write (`before_send_failed`). Nothing is sent in any of these cases, and `--allow-send` on the MCP server does not skip the check.
- The check guards drafts, not the process running correspond: whoever sets its environment or edits the config file (`$CORRESPOND_CONFIG` can point at another file) chooses the check. Commands that write without correspond (`gh issue comment`, say) are covered by liaise’s hook, not by this check.
- A write that fails is a result, not an exception: `ok: false`, an `error_kind` (`auth`, `permission`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `network`, `validation`, `unavailable`, `unconfirmed`, or one of the four check kinds above), and whether a retry can help (`retryable`, `retry_after`).
- **`--idempotency-key KEY` (`idempotency_key=` in Python) keeps a message from going out twice.** A channel can post and then fail (the platform took the message, and its answer never came), so a retry would post it again. With a key, correspond remembers what the key did (under the data root, in `sends/`): the same key after a send that went out posts nothing and returns that result. After a failure that may have posted (`network`, `unavailable`, a crash), it reads the conversation back for its own message with the same text and returns it if found. If it cannot confirm, it sends nothing and fails with `unconfirmed`: check the conversation, then send with a new key. A key reused for a different message is refused (`validation`). Nothing is added to the posted text. Two processes sending with the same key at the same moment are not covered.
- `-` as the text reads it from stdin; `--json` prints the whole result.

## Listening

```bash
correspond listen github:owner/repo    # issue, comment, review comment and discussion activity since the last listen
correspond listen email: --peek        # look without moving the cursor
```

Cursors live under the data root, one per reference. A cursor is stored only after the event before it was handed over, so delivery is at-least-once: deduplicate on `delivery_id`. The first listen looks back a day. Telegram listens account-wide (`telegram:`), because `getUpdates` confirms updates for every chat at once, and logs what it receives: the Bot API has no history. On a server, Telegram can push instead: install `correspond[server]` and run `correspond-telegram-webhook` behind your HTTPS reverse proxy. It binds `127.0.0.1` (another address only with `webhook_allow_remote`), and the receiver stores nothing that lacks the `webhook_secret`, in arrival order. Run `correspond set-webhook telegram https://... --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run` (one connection at a time), set `delivery = "webhook"`, and `listen telegram:` reads what the receiver stored; `correspond webhook-info telegram` says where updates go now. The receiver keeps updates under the data root, or in the store `webhook_store = "module:attr"` names (an `s3dol` store on a server, say). Telegram serves `getUpdates` or a webhook, never both: `correspond delete-webhook telegram` returns to polling. GitHub has no `since` filter for discussions, so a reply that does not move its discussion’s activity can be missed by polling; a `discussion_comment` webhook closes that gap: run `correspond-github-webhook` the same way (`127.0.0.1:8082`), add a repository or organization webhook (content type `application/json`, the `webhook_secret`, the “Discussion comments” event) pointing at your proxy, and set `delivery = "webhook"` under `[github]`. The receiver verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` and keeps only which discussion had a comment; listen still polls, and also reads those discussions whole. Slack can push too, through its Events API: run `correspond-slack-events` the same way (`127.0.0.1:8083`), give your proxy’s URL as the app’s Event Subscriptions Request URL (bot events `message.channels`, and `message.groups` for private channels), and set `delivery = "events"` under `[slack]`. The receiver checks every request’s `X-Slack-Signature` with the `signing_secret` (five-minute window), answers Slack’s `url_verification`, and keeps the `message` events; listen then reads them instead of polling, edits (`message.updated`) and deletions (`message.deleted`) included.

## Configuration

`correspond requirements <channel>` lists everything a channel reads: each setting’s environment variable, what it is, where to get it, and where its value currently comes from (`env`, `keychain`, `config`, `default`, `missing`), never the value.

- **Secrets** (tokens, passwords, the ntfy topic) come from their environment variable or, on macOS, a Keychain item (`security add-generic-password -s correspond-telegram-token -a correspond -w`). They are never read from the config file.
- **Other settings** may also go in `~/.config/correspond/config.toml` (or `$CORRESPOND_CONFIG`), one table per channel:
  ```toml
  [email]
  imap_host = "imap.example.org"
  smtp_host = "smtp.example.org"
  trusted_authserv_ids = ["mx.example.org"]
  own_domains = ["example.org"]           # recipients elsewhere are external
  lists = ["@lists.example.org"]          # list addresses, or a whole list server

  [ntfy]
  topic_keychain_service = "my-ntfy-topic"
  denies_anonymous_read = true            # only if your server's auth-default-access denies reads
  cache_duration = "12h"
  ```
- **`before_send`**, at the top of the config file (before any table), names the check every write runs, as `"module:attr"`. The check is a callable `before_send(ref, draft, audience, *, operation, dry_run, message_id, **context)`. It returns to let the write go ahead, or raises `correspond.errors.Refused(reason, **details)` or `correspond.errors.NeedsApproval(reason, **details)`. Accept `**context`, so that later context keys do not break it. liaise supplies one:
  ```toml
  before_send = "liaise.vet:before_send"
  ```

  It is imported when a write first needs it. Leave it out and the default (`correspond.outbound:notice`) only shows the audience. A `before_send` key inside a table is refused rather than ignored. A Python caller can pass `before_send=` to the write functions instead; the command line and the MCP tools cannot.
- **State** (cursors, the Telegram log, web inbox reports) lives under `~/.local/share/correspond/` (or `$CORRESPOND_DATA_DIR`), one folder per kind, never in a repository.

## The web inbox

A web page posts feedback to a small ASGI collector; `webinbox:<site>` reads what it stored. The app binds nothing itself: run it on localhost behind your own server.

```bash
pip install uvicorn
export CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_SITES=example-site CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_ORIGINS=https://app.example.org
export CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_SECRET=...   # shared with the host application's server
uvicorn --factory correspond.channels.webinbox:app_from_env --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

The rate limit applies per visitor address. uvicorn already reports the visitor for a proxy on the same host (its `--forwarded-allow-ips` default); for a proxy elsewhere, set `CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` to the number of proxies in front, or every visitor shares the proxy’s limit. Forwarded addresses are believed only from a non-public connection, and IPv6 visitors are limited per /64. Several sites on one collector need a secret each, `CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_SECRET_<SITE>` (the site name upper-cased, `-` as `_`) or a Keychain item `correspond-webinbox-secret-<site>`, so that no site’s server can sign identities for another. The shared `CORRESPOND_WEBINBOX_SECRET` serves a single site only, and `correspond requirements webinbox` reports a configuration the collector would refuse.

`POST /example-site/reports` takes JSON with a required `text` and optional `name`, `email`, `page`, `context`, `attachments` (base64, stored by SHA-256, referenced rather than inlined) and `identity`. Without `identity` a report is `claimed`. The host application’s server can sign its logged-in user, which makes the report `bound`:

```python
from correspond.channels.webinbox import sign_identity

identity = sign_identity(
    secret, "example-site", user_id, name=display_name
)  # put this in the page
```

Any server language can do the same: HMAC-SHA256, hex, over the lines `v1`, site, issued-at (Unix seconds), user id, name, email. An invalid or expired signature is refused (401) and nothing is stored. The collector also enforces the origin allowlist (with CORS preflight), a per-client rate limit, and size and media-type limits.

## Routing

```python
from correspond import metadata_rule, route

decision = route(
    message,
    bindings={
        "github:example/app?labels=partner:*": "subject:app"
    },  # 1. where it arrived
    threads={"github:example/app#12": "case:7"},  # 2. what it continues
    rules=[metadata_rule("queue:urgent", labels="priority:high")],  # 3. what it carries
    classifier=None,  # 4. optional, last
)
decision.target, decision.rule, decision.reason
```

The rules are yours; correspond runs them in that order and says which one decided. Nothing matched returns `None`: the message is unrouted. Check bindings when you load them: `check_binding(pattern)` lists what would make one never match, such as an unknown channel, or `?label=` where GitHub messages carry `labels`.

## Python

```python
import correspond

messages = correspond.read("github:octocat/hello-world#1")
messages[0].author.handle, messages[0].authenticity.grade

result = correspond.send(
    "email:someone@example.org", "It is fixed.", title="The export", dry_run=True
)
result.plan

for event in correspond.listen("webinbox:example-site"):
    ...

correspond.register_channel(
    MyChannel()
)  # anything with name, capabilities, parse_ref and the operations it has
```

`correspond.testing.FakeChannel` is an in-memory channel for tests, and `python -m correspond.testing` runs the CLI with it registered as `fake`.

## What the sender actually wrote

A reply body carries the whole conversation beneath it, so anything built from raw bodies (a summary, a profile, a search) mostly measures the people being quoted. `correspond.authored` keeps the sender’s own words:

```python
from correspond.authored import authored, authored_thread

found = authored(body)
found.text, found.signature, found.quoted, found.forwarded

# Answers written inside the quote ("Responses below.") need the earlier messages:
for part in authored_thread([first_body, reply_body]):
    part.full_text  # top text + recovered inline answers
```

It recognises reply headers in English, French, German, Swedish, Spanish, Italian and Dutch clients (Gmail’s `On … wrote:`, Outlook’s `From: … Sent: …` block, `-----Original Message-----`), forwards, mobile footers, contact blocks after the sign-off, and legal disclaimers; the sign-off itself stays in the text. Other vocabularies go in through `markers=`. On the CLI: `correspond authored - < body.txt` and `correspond authored-thread thread.json --author someone@`.

## MCP

```bash
pip install "correspond[mcp]"
```

```json
{"mcpServers": {"correspond": {"command": "correspond-mcp"}}}
```

The server exposes the reading tools. The writes (`send`, `edit`, `react`, `upload`, and the rest) are exposed only when the operator starts it with `correspond-mcp --allow-send`, and still take `dry_run`. The data root is the server’s, never the model’s.

## Claude Code channel

`correspond-channel` (same `mcp` extra) is an MCP server that pushes new messages on the conversations you name into a running Claude Code session, as a [channel](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference). Each new message from an allowlisted sender arrives as `<channel source="correspond" channel="github" conversation="github:example/demo#1" message_id="..." sender="github:ada" grade="platform">text</channel>`; replies are the ordinary correspond tools (`send` with `ref` = the conversation and `reply_to` = the message id), with the writes exposed only under `--allow-send` and dry-run first, exactly as in `correspond-mcp`.

```json
{"mcpServers": {"correspond": {"command": "correspond-channel",
  "args": ["github:example/demo#1", "--allow", "github:ada", "--allow-send"]}}}
```

```bash
# a channel that is not a plugin on the approved list loads with the development flag
claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:correspond
```

- **Senders**: only senders on `--allow` (the attested address, `github:ada`, or `<channel>:<native id>`) are forwarded; an empty allowlist forwards nothing unless `--allow-any-sender`. A `forged` message, the account’s own messages and senderless events (a bare reaction) are never forwarded.
- **Permission relay**: `--relay-to <ref>` (needs `--allow-send`) declares `claude/channel/permission`, sends each tool-approval prompt to that conversation, and turns a reply `yes <id>` / `no <id>` there into a verdict. Only a sender on the explicit allowlist whose grade is authenticated (`platform`, `domain`, `bound`, `crypto`; `--approve-grades` narrows it) can approve, and only an id the server relayed. Use a conversation only you can read: the prompt carries the tool’s arguments. The approver must be a **different account** from the one correspond sends as: the account’s own messages are never forwarded (otherwise Claude could post `yes <id>` and approve itself), and the server logs it when it drops one from an allowlisted sender. Only a newly created message approves; an edited one never does.
- **Polling and state**: every `--interval` seconds (default 30), with its own cursors under `<data root>/channel-cursors/` so it never takes events from `correspond listen`; events are deduplicated on their delivery id. The flags can also live in a `[claude_channel]` table of the config file (`refs`, `allow`, `relay_to`, `approve_grades`, `interval`, `allow_any_sender`).

## Agent skill

A `correspond` skill ships inside the package (`correspond/data/skills/correspond/`): how to read without taking instructions from message text, what each grade permits, and how to write safely (dry run, operator approval, no private content in public places). Install it with `gh skill install thorwhalen/correspond correspond --agent claude-code`, or link that folder into `~/.claude/skills/`.

## Design

The seams, surfaces and deliberate non-seams are in [Discussion #1](https://github.com/thorwhalen/correspond/discussions/1).

# _autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md

# correspond.authored

What the sender of an email actually wrote: their text, apart from quoted replies, forwarded blocks, signatures and disclaimers.

A reply body carries the whole conversation beneath it, so a profile, a summary or a search
built from raw bodies mostly measures the people being quoted. [`authored()`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.authored) splits one
body into its parts:

```pycon
>>> body = '''Fine by me, ship it Friday.
...
... /Ada
...
... On Mon, 3 Mar 2025 at 10:00, Grace Hopper <grace@example.org> wrote:
... > Can we ship on Friday?
... '''
>>> found = authored(body)
>>> found.text
'Fine by me, ship it Friday.\n\n/Ada'
>>> found.quoted.splitlines()[-1]
'> Can we ship on Friday?'
```

Three shapes are handled:

- **top-posting**: the text above the first reply header (`On … wrote:` in several
  languages, an Outlook `From: … Sent: …` block, `-----Original Message-----`) or above
  a run of `>` lines;
- **forwarding**: a forwarded block is never authored text (`forwarded` is set);
- **inline replies**: answers written *inside* the quoted text with no `>` marker, as
  Outlook users do (“Responses below.”). These are recovered only when the earlier messages
  of the thread are passed as `earlier`: a line of the quoted region that appears in none
  of them was written by this sender. [`authored_thread()`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.authored_thread) does that for a whole thread.

Signatures (after 

```
``
```

– 

```
``
```

, a mobile footer, or a contact block after the sign-off) and legal
disclaimers are split off; the sign-off itself (“Best,”, “/Ada”) stays in the text, since it
is part of how the person writes.

The reply-header and footer vocabulary is a seam: pass `markers=` a [`Markers`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.Markers) with
other patterns. The defaults cover English, French, German, Swedish, Spanish, Italian and
Dutch clients. Prior art: `email-reply-parser` (top-posting, English) and
`mail-parser-reply` (multilingual headers); neither recovers inline replies.

| [`authored`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.authored)(text, \*[, earlier, markers, ...])   | Split one email body (plain text) into what its sender wrote and everything else.                                                                |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Split one email body (plain text) into what its sender wrote and everything else.

`earlier` is the text of messages that came before it in the thread (raw bodies are
fine); with it, answers written inside the quoted text are recovered into `inline`.
Only the quoted copy of the message being replied to (not the older history beneath it)
can hold them, and only when one earlier message is found in that copy (at least
`min_coverage` of its own lines), since a thread missing its earlier messages would make
every quoted line look new. Earlier text pasted back with no header counts as quoted.

```pycon
>>> authored("Thanks!\n\n-- \nAda Lovelace\nAnalytical Engines Ltd").signature
'--\nAda Lovelace\nAnalytical Engines Ltd'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Authored`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.Authored)

[`authored()`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.authored) for each body of a thread, oldest first, each given every earlier body as `earlier`.

```pycon
>>> first, second = authored_thread([
...     "Can we ship Friday?\nAnd who writes the notes?",
...     "Answers below.\n\nFrom: Ada <ada@example.org>\nSent: Monday\n"
...     "Can we ship Friday?\nYes, Friday works.\nAnd who writes the notes?\nGrace does.",
... ])
>>> second.inline
('Yes, Friday works.', 'Grace does.')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Authored`](_autosummary/correspond.authored.html.md#correspond.authored.Authored)]


# _autosummary/correspond.channel.html.md

# correspond.channel

Serve listeners as a Claude Code channel: new messages pushed into a running session, replies through the ordinary tools.

Run `correspond-channel` (install the extra first: `pip install "correspond[mcp]"`). It
is an MCP stdio server that declares `experimental['claude/channel']`, polls
[`correspond.listen()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.listen) for the conversations it was given, and emits one
`notifications/claude/channel` per new message, from an allowlisted sender, as:

```default
{"content": "<the text>",
 "meta": {"channel": "github", "conversation": "github:example/demo#1",
          "message_id": "...", "sender": "github:ada", "grade": "platform"}}
```

which Claude sees as `<channel source="correspond" channel="github" ...>text</channel>`.
Meta keys are identifiers only (Claude Code silently drops a key with a hyphen).

**Replies are the ordinary correspond tools** ([`correspond.tools`](_autosummary/correspond.tools.html.md#module-correspond.tools), through
[`correspond.mcp.mk_server()`](_autosummary/correspond.mcp.html.md#correspond.mcp.mk_server)): the reads by default, the writes only with
`--allow-send`, each write dry-run first and through the operator’s `before_send` check.

**Senders.** Only messages from senders on the allowlist (`--allow github:ada`, matched on
the sender’s attested address or `<channel>:<native id>`, never the room) are forwarded;
an empty allowlist forwards nothing unless `--allow-any-sender` opens it. A `forged`
message is never forwarded, the bot’s own messages never loop back, and events without an
attested sender (a bare reaction) are not forwarded.

**Permission relay** (`claude/channel/permission`). With `--relay-to <ref>` (which needs
`--allow-send`, because relaying is a send) the server declares the permission capability;
each `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` is sent to that conversation as a
prompt ending in `Reply "yes <id>" or "no <id>"`; and a reply in that conversation of
that shape becomes a `notifications/claude/channel/permission` verdict, never chat, but
only when its sender is on the explicit allowlist (`--allow-any-sender` does not count),
its authenticity grade is one of [`APPROVE_GRADES`](_autosummary/correspond.channel.html.md#correspond.channel.APPROVE_GRADES) (authenticated: not `claimed` or
`forged`), and the id is one this server relayed and has not yet answered.

How the Python MCP SDK does this (`mcp` 1.27, `fastmcp` 3.3, verified by the tests):

- *Declaring the capability*: the low-level `mcp.server.lowlevel.Server` takes it as
  `create_initialization_options(experimental_capabilities={"claude/channel": {}})`;
  FastMCP (what `py2mcp` builds) keeps a public `experimental_capabilities` dict that its
  low-level server merges into the same call. This module sets that dict.
- *Emitting a custom method*: `ServerSession.send_notification` only `model_dump``s its
  argument into a ``JSONRPCNotification`, so any model with `method` and `params`
  (`mcp.types.Notification`) goes out unvalidated. A background task has no session handle
  in FastMCP, so this module writes the same `SessionMessage(JSONRPCNotification(...))` onto
  the transport’s write stream, after the client’s `notifications/initialized`.
- *Receiving a custom method*: the SDK validates incoming notifications against the closed
  `ClientNotification` union and drops anything else with a warning, so
  `permission_request` is taken off the read stream by a tap in front of the session.

### Module Attributes

### correspond.channel.APPROVE_GRADES *= frozenset({Grade.BOUND, Grade.CRYPTO, Grade.DOMAIN, Grade.PLATFORM})*

the authenticated ones.

* **Type:**
  Grades whose sender may approve tool use

### correspond.channel.CURSOR_KIND *= 'channel-cursors'*

Where the channel server keeps its listen cursors, apart from `correspond listen`’s.

### correspond.channel.FORWARD_GRADES *= frozenset({Grade.BOUND, Grade.CLAIMED, Grade.CRYPTO, Grade.DOMAIN, Grade.PLATFORM})*

everything but a failed verification.

* **Type:**
  Grades forwarded by default

### *class* correspond.channel.Gate(allow=frozenset({}), allow_any=False, forward_grades=frozenset({Grade.BOUND, Grade.CLAIMED, Grade.CRYPTO, Grade.DOMAIN, Grade.PLATFORM}), approve_grades=frozenset({Grade.BOUND, Grade.CRYPTO, Grade.DOMAIN, Grade.PLATFORM}), relay_to=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Who gets through, as a pure policy: the allowlist, the grades forwarded, and who may approve.

`allow` holds sender addresses (`github:ada`) or `<channel>:<native id>`; empty
forwards nothing unless `allow_any`. `relay_to` is the canonical relay conversation
(verdicts are read there only); approval needs the explicit allowlist and a grade in
`approve_grades`, which may hold only authenticated grades.

#### allowed(event)

Whether this event’s sender may put text in front of Claude.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### may_approve(event)

Whether this event’s sender may answer a permission prompt: allowlisted by name and authenticated.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### route(event, , pending=None)

The notification an event becomes (a channel message or a verdict), or `None` when it is dropped.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channel.META_KEYS *= ('channel', 'conversation', 'message_id', 'sender', 'grade')*

identifiers only.

* **Type:**
  The `meta` keys of every channel notification, in order

### correspond.channel.channel_notification(event)

The `notifications/claude/channel` message for one event that carries a message.

```pycon
>>> from correspond.testing import demo_message
>>> note = channel_notification(Event(kind="message.created", channel="fake", delivery_id="d1",
...                                   message=demo_message()))
>>> note["method"], note["params"]["content"]
('notifications/claude/channel', 'The export drops the last row.')
>>> note["params"]["meta"]
{'channel': 'fake', 'conversation': 'fake:example/demo', 'message_id': 'm1', 'sender': 'fake:ada', 'grade': 'platform'}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### correspond.channel.main(argv=None)

Serve the channel over stdio (see `options()` for the arguments).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channel.notifications(refs, \*, gate, cursors=None, registry=None, seen=None, pending=None, limit=None, seen_limit=10000, log=<function \_log>)

One poll of every ref: the notifications its new events become, deduplicated on delivery id.

Lazy on purpose: [`correspond.listen()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.listen) stores an event’s cursor only when the next one
is asked for, so a consumer that emits each notification before asking for the next one
gets at-least-once delivery, and `seen` makes it once per process. A ref that fails is
logged and skipped; the others are still polled.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### correspond.channel.parse_verdict(text)

`("allow" | "deny", request_id)` for a reply like `yes abcde`, else `None`.

```pycon
>>> parse_verdict("Yes ABCDE"), parse_verdict("no qwxyz"), parse_verdict("yes"), parse_verdict("yes hello")
(('allow', 'abcde'), ('deny', 'qwxyz'), None, None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channel.permission_prompt(params)

The text sent to the relay conversation for one permission request.

```pycon
>>> print(permission_prompt({"request_id": "abcde", "tool_name": "Bash",
...                          "description": "List files", "input_preview": '{"command": "ls"}'}))
Claude wants to run Bash: List files
{"command": "ls"}

Reply "yes abcde" or "no abcde"
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### correspond.channel.serve(\*\*kwargs)

Run the channel over stdio until the client goes away; `kwargs` as for [`serve_streams()`](_autosummary/correspond.channel.html.md#correspond.channel.serve_streams).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *async* correspond.channel.serve_streams(read_stream, write_stream, \*, refs, gate, allow_send=False, interval=30.0, cursors=None, registry=None, send=None, server=None, log=<function \_log>)

Run the channel over a pair of MCP message streams (stdio in [`serve()`](_autosummary/correspond.channel.html.md#correspond.channel.serve), memory in tests).

`server` defaults to [`correspond.mcp.mk_server()`](_autosummary/correspond.mcp.html.md#correspond.mcp.mk_server) with the channel instructions;
`send` (the relay’s outbound) defaults to [`correspond.send()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.send) on `registry`.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channel.verdict_notification(request_id, behavior)

The `notifications/claude/channel/permission` message carrying a verdict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.apprise.html.md

# correspond.channels.apprise

Apprise: send-only notifications to the long tail of services (about 155), each named by an alias.

### References

`apprise:<alias>`, an alias being 1-64 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` (case is
folded; `all` and `always` are Apprise’s match-everything tags, so they are refused). A
reference never holds an Apprise URL, because the URL
carries the service’s credentials (`discord://webhook_id/webhook_token`,
`tgram://bot_token/chat_id`…). The alias is resolved, in this order:

1. `$CORRESPOND_APPRISE_URL_<ALIAS>` (upper case, `-` as `_`), holding ONE URL;
2. on macOS, the Keychain item `correspond-apprise-url-<alias>`, likewise;
3. the local Apprise configuration file named by `config` in the `[apprise]` table (or
   `$CORRESPOND_APPRISE_CONFIG`), where the alias is an Apprise **tag**: every URL in the
   file carrying exactly that tag is notified (see the configuration-file documentation
   linked from [https://pypi.org/project/apprise/](https://pypi.org/project/apprise/)). URLs tagged `always` are NOT added:
   an alias names its recipients, and a typo must not reach anyone.

A dry run reads only the environment and the config file: a Keychain alias is looked up when
sending, and the plan says so. The plan names the service (the URL’s scheme), never the URL,
and Apprise’s own logging, which prints URLs, is silenced while correspond calls it.

Needs the `apprise` extra: `pip install "correspond[apprise]"`. It is imported when a
message is sent, not when the channel is listed.

```pycon
>>> Apprise().parse_ref("team-alerts").kind
'alias'
```

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.discord.html.md

# correspond.channels.discord

Discord: a bot reading and posting in channels over REST, through discorddol.

Reference: `discord:<channel id>`, a channel or a thread (Discord numbers both with
snowflakes). A bot reads only the channels its server roles let it see, and since Discord
made message content a privileged intent, it reads the text of a message only when the
Message Content intent is enabled for it (Developer Portal, Bot, Privileged Gateway
Intents; a bot in more than 100 servers needs Discord’s approval) or when the message
mentions it.

- `read` fetches the channel’s history (the latest 50 messages unless `limit` says).
- `listen` polls the channel for messages newer than the last one seen (the cursor is
  that message’s id; a first poll looks back a day): new messages, not edits or
  deletions. With `listen_via = "gateway"` it opens the gateway for a short window
  instead and reports new, edited and deleted messages; the cursor is the gateway session,
  which the next listen resumes (Discord replays what was missed) rather than identifying
  again, since 1,000 identifies in a day reset the bot token.
- `send` posts a message (2,000 characters at most); a title is prepended in bold. With
  `reply_to` it is a Discord reply to that message (its author is not pinged). Only
  the users it mentions as `<@id>` are pinged: `@everyone`, `@here` and role
  mentions stay text, through Discord’s allowed mentions.
- `verify` grades an HTTP interaction Discord posted to your endpoint: `crypto` when
  its Ed25519 signature (`X-Signature-Ed25519` over `X-Signature-Timestamp` + body)
  checks against the application’s public key, `forged` otherwise. Discord sends
  deliberately invalid signatures to test the endpoint; those must come back `forged`
  (answer them 401).

Senders are `platform`: Discord authenticated the account, and correspond fetched the
message from the API itself. A server member’s role ids are its `authority`. The bot token never appears in an error or a plan.

Needs the `discord` extra (discorddol, over discord.py in REST-only mode), imported on
first use, not when the channel is listed.

```pycon
>>> Discord().parse_ref("123456789012345678").encoded
'discord:123456789012345678'
```

### Classes

| [`Discord`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.discord.html.md#correspond.channels.discord.Discord)(\*[, backend, http, run, clock, gateway])   | A Discord bot over REST: read a channel, poll it for new messages, post to it.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* correspond.channels.discord.Discord(\*, backend=None, http=<function urllib_http>, run=<function run>, clock=<built-in function time>, gateway=<function gateway_window>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The channel is looked up once per reference. When it cannot be (no lookup in
this backend, or Discord refused), the answer is the wider server group.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* backend *: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*

discorddol’s REST backend with the configured bot token, or the one passed in.

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

A bot’s view of Discord, over REST.

#### parse_ref(id)

A channel or thread id.

* **Return type:**
  [`ConversationRef`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.ConversationRef)

#### poll(ref, , cursor=None, limit=None)

Messages newer than `cursor` (a message id), oldest first; a first poll looks back a day.

With `listen_via = "gateway"`, one gateway window instead (see the module docstring).

#### read(ref, , since=None, limit=None)

The channel’s latest messages (`limit`, else 50), oldest first; with `since`, only those after it.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message)]

#### verify(headers, body)

`crypto` when `X-Signature-Ed25519` checks over a fresh `X-Signature-Timestamp` + body, `forged` otherwise.

Raises [`MissingRequirement`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.MissingRequirement) when the public key is unset
or unusable (a configuration error, never a verdict on the request). Replay
protection is the five-minute window only: a captured request can be replayed
within it, so act idempotently on an interaction’s id.

* **Return type:**
  [`Authenticity`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Authenticity)


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.gdrive.html.md

# correspond.channels.gdrive

Google Drive: a shared folder, read only, where files that a conversation announces arrive.

A message often says “uploaded, it’s the one dated Tuesday” about a file that is not
attached to it: the folder is the payload and the message is the notification. This
channel lets one facade read both ends. It reads, and does nothing else: no listening, no
writing.

Reference: `gdrive:<folder id>` (a folder’s URL, `https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<id>`,
is accepted and normalised to its id).

`read` returns one [`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message) per file in the folder and its
subfolders: the text is the file’s path in the folder, `sent_at` its last modification,
the author Drive’s last modifying user, and the file itself the message’s one
[`Attachment`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Attachment), fetched only on `content()`. So `since` and
`limit` mean what they mean everywhere, and “the file Ada mentioned on Tuesday” lines up
with “the file modified on Tuesday”. A Google Docs, Sheets or Slides file has no bytes of its
own; its attachment says so when fetched.

Credentials are the host’s: a service-account key file named by `service_account_file`,
used with the read-only Drive scope (share the folder with the account’s `client_email`),
or an authenticated PyDrive2 `GoogleDrive` passed as `drive=`. Needs the `gdrive`
extra (pydrivedol), imported on first use, not when the channel is listed.

```pycon
>>> GoogleDrive().parse_ref("https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp?usp=sharing").encoded
'gdrive:0AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`READONLY_SCOPE`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.gdrive.html.md#correspond.channels.gdrive.READONLY_SCOPE)   | it never writes to Drive.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|

| [`GoogleDrive`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.gdrive.html.md#correspond.channels.gdrive.GoogleDrive)(\*[, drive, run, max_depth])   | A Drive folder, read only: its files as messages, each carrying the file as an attachment.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

#### audience(ref, , draft=None)

`anyone` (with or without the link) makes it public; a domain, the organisation;
otherwise the users it is shared with, by address, and each group as a class whose
members are not listed. Anyone who can read a file can download and keep a copy.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

#### *property* drive *: [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)*

* **Type:**
  The authenticated PyDrive2 `GoogleDrive`

#### parse_ref(id)

The folder’s files, oldest modification first, one message each; `since` is asked of Drive.
