# _autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md

# correspond.channels.github

GitHub: issues, pull request conversations and discussions, through the `gh` CLI.

correspond never holds a GitHub token: every call is `gh api`, authenticated as whatever
account `gh` is logged in as on this machine, so writes act as that user. Request bodies
go to `gh` on stdin, never on its command line, so a long comment cannot hit the argument
limit and never shows in the process table.

### References

- `github:owner/repo`: the repository. `read` lists recent open issues and pull
  requests, `listen` polls its issue, comment, review comment and discussion activity,
  `send` opens an issue (a title is required), or a discussion when `Draft.native`
  names a `category`.
- `github:owner/repo#N`: an issue, a pull request, or a discussion. GitHub numbers the
  three in one sequence; correspond asks which. Reading or listening to a pull request
  includes its review comments on the diff, each threaded under the comment that opened
  its thread (`reply_to`), and a reply to one of them joins that thread.
  `label` and `unlabel` work on an issue
  or pull request only: GitHub discussions have categories, not labels. `close` and
  `reopen` work on all three: an issue or pull request through `PATCH .../issues/N`,
  a discussion through GraphQL `closeDiscussion` / `reopenDiscussion`. Each kind
  takes its own close reasons (issue: `completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`;
  discussion: `resolved`, `outdated`, `duplicate`, with `completed` accepted as
  `resolved`).

Opening an issue takes `Draft.native` keys `labels`, `assignees` and `milestone`,
set in the creating request so watchers are notified once. GitHub silently drops an
assignee who cannot be assigned, so the plan reports what the created issue actually
carries (`landed`) and what did not stick (`not_applied`). `Draft.native`
`category` (a discussion category’s name or slug) opens a discussion instead, through
GraphQL `createDiscussion`; it takes none of the issue fields.

Message ids match the anchors in GitHub’s own URLs: `issue-N` (the opening post of issue
or pull request N), `issuecomment-ID`, `discussion_rID` (a review comment on a pull
request’s diff), `discussion-N`, `discussioncomment-ID`.

Messages read through the API are `platform` (GitHub authenticated the account), with the
author’s `author_association` (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `CONTRIBUTOR`, `NONE`, …) as
`authority`. A webhook delivery is graded by [`GitHub.verify()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub.verify): `crypto` when its
`X-Hub-Signature-256` matches the configured secret, `forged` otherwise.

[`GitHub.audience()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub.audience) says who can read a conversation: the repository’s readership,
from its visibility, and its collaborators when the account may list them.

```pycon
>>> GitHub().parse_ref("OctoCat/Hello-World#1").encoded
'github:octocat/hello-world#1'
>>> signature("a-secret", b"{}")
'sha256=...'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`WATCHERS`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.WATCHERS)   | Reader classes of a repository that cannot be listed, as [`GitHub.audience()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub.audience) words them.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`signature`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.signature)(secret, body)   | The `X-Hub-Signature-256` value GitHub sends for `body` under `secret`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`GitHub`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub)(\*[, run, gh, recent_discussions, ...])   | GitHub through `gh`: read, listen, send, edit, react, verify webhook deliveries, and say who reads a conversation.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* correspond.channels.github.GitHub(\*, run=<function run>, gh='gh', recent_discussions=3, deliveries=None, clock=<built-in function time_ns>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

GitHub through `gh`: read, listen, send, edit, react, verify webhook deliveries, and say who reads a conversation.

#### audience(ref, , draft=None)

Who can read a repository’s issues, pull requests and discussions, asked of GitHub now.

Every conversation in a repository has the repository’s readership. A draft changes
nothing: a mention decides who is notified, not who can read. One
`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` call gives the visibility and the owner’s type:

- `public`: scope `public`; readers are not listed.
- `private`: scope `named` when a user owns it, `org` otherwise.
- `internal`: scope `org`, with every member of the enterprise as a class.
- a 404 or a 403: `public`, defaulted. GitHub answers 404 both for a repository
  that does not exist and for one the account cannot see.

For a private or internal repository, collaborators (team members, members reading
through the base permission, and owners included) are listed only when the account
can write to it, since GitHub lists them to no one else. The list is a lower bound
and the audience is never `complete`: installed apps and webhooks read the
repository without being listable through `gh`, and an organisation’s
security-manager teams read every repository. An organisation’s base permission is
read when the account may see it (owners only), and otherwise assumed to be the
documented default, read; `read`, `write` and `admin` reach the same readers
and give the same class. The `gh` account itself is never consulted, so the answer,
and its hash, do not depend on who asks. Every repository emails bodies to watchers
and participants, and nothing sent is retractable. Nothing is cached. A rate limit or
a transport failure raises; [`correspond.ops.audience()`](_autosummary/correspond.ops.html.md#correspond.ops.audience) resolves it to public.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

Issues, pull request conversations and discussions.

#### close(ref, , reason=None, dry_run=False)

Close an issue or pull request (`PATCH .../issues/N`) or a discussion (GraphQL).

`reason` is the kind’s own: an issue’s `state_reason` (`completed`,
`not_planned`, `duplicate`) or a discussion’s (`resolved`, `outdated`,
`duplicate`; `completed` is accepted as `resolved`); a pull request takes
none. The plan reads the state back: `was` (before) and `now` /
`now_reason` (what the response says), so closing an already-closed
conversation is visible as such.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### *property* deliveries *: [MutableMapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*

What the webhook receiver stored (read when `delivery` is `webhook`).

#### edit(ref, message_id, draft, , dry_run=False)

Replace the body of an issue, a comment, a review comment, a discussion or a discussion comment.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### label(ref, labels, , dry_run=False)

Add labels to an issue or pull request (`POST .../labels`).

GitHub creates a label that does not already exist in the repository rather than
rejecting it, so `landed` in the plan is mostly a confirmation: the requested
names the response’s own (now-current) label list actually carries, which is read
back and reported the way an assignee is not (a login that is not a member of the
repository is silently dropped from `assignees`; a label name never is). The
response lists every label now on the issue, including ones this call never
mentioned, so `landed` is filtered to the requested names, not the full list.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### parse_ref(id)

`owner/repo` or `owner/repo#N`, lower-cased (GitHub names are case-insensitive).

* **Return type:**
  [`ConversationRef`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.ConversationRef)

#### poll(ref, , cursor=None, limit=None)

Issue, comment, review comment, review and discussion activity since `cursor`; a first poll looks back a day.

The cursor is opaque JSON: the update time the next poll starts from (`t`; GitHub’s
`since` includes it), the creation time from which an issue still counts as new
(`l`, which stays behind while the issues list is being read in parts), and the
events already delivered at `t` (`seen`). So neither `limit` nor several changes
within one second can make a poll repeat itself, and a list cut short (more than
`MAX_PAGES` pages changed) is resumed from where it was cut. A bare ISO time is also
accepted as a cursor.

Discussions have no `since` filter, so a repository’s are walked newest activity
first until a page reaches one older than the cursor (`_active_discussions()`),
and each active one is read whole; one discussion is read whole on every poll. A
discussion counts as new when it was created at or after the cursor, and a
discussion comment is `message.updated` when it was created before it.

#### prepare(ref, draft)

The draft as it will post: `notify` handles checked, the missing mentions added. Pure.

* **Return type:**
  [`Draft`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Draft)

#### react(ref, message_id, reaction, , dry_run=False)

Add one of `REACTIONS` to an issue, a comment, a review comment, a discussion or a discussion comment.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### read(ref, , since=None, limit=None)

An issue, pull request or discussion with its comments; for a repository, recent open issues and pull requests.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message)]

#### reopen(ref, , dry_run=False)

Reopen a closed issue, pull request or discussion; the plan reads the state back as for [`close()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub.close).

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### send(ref, draft, , dry_run=False)

Comment on an issue, pull request or discussion; on a repository, open an issue (`title` required), or a discussion with native `category`.

`draft.reply_to` answers a discussion comment, or a review comment on a pull
request’s diff (`discussion_rID`), joining its thread.

`draft.notify` handles (`octocat`, `org/team`) the text does not @mention yet
are mentioned on a closing `cc` line, which GitHub notifies; the plan lists them
under `mentions_added`.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### unlabel(ref, labels, , dry_run=False)

Remove labels from an issue or pull request.

GitHub has no bulk removal: one `DELETE .../labels/{name}` per label. A label
already absent from the issue answers 404 the same way a missing issue does, so the
issue’s existence is checked first (`_require_issue()`) and every 404 after that
is read as “was not on the issue”, not as an error.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### verify(headers, body)

`crypto` when `X-Hub-Signature-256` matches the webhook secret, `forged` otherwise.

* **Return type:**
  [`Authenticity`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Authenticity)

### correspond.channels.github.WATCHERS *= 'watchers and participants receive the body by email'*

Reader classes of a repository that cannot be listed, as [`GitHub.audience()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#correspond.channels.github.GitHub.audience) words them.

### correspond.channels.github.signature(secret, body)

The `X-Hub-Signature-256` value GitHub sends for `body` under `secret`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md

# correspond.channels.github_webhook

GitHub webhook receiver: `discussion_comment` deliveries, so listen sees every discussion reply.

GitHub has no `since` filter for discussions, so a poll walks them by latest activity
and can miss a reply that moves neither the discussion’s `updatedAt` nor its place in
that order (when the discussion is outside the `recent_discussions` window). A
`discussion_comment` webhook names every such discussion as it happens.

[`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.mk_webhook_app) is the receiver, an ASGI app that checks `X-Hub-Signature-256`
against the `webhook_secret` (the HMAC over the body: nothing unsigned is stored) and
keeps, under the data root (`github-webhook/`), only which discussion of which
repository had a comment, and when it arrived. With `delivery = "webhook"` in the
`github` config, `listen` still polls, and also reads whole every discussion the
receiver saw since the cursor, finding the reply by its own creation time: the webhook
is a hint, the poll stays the source of the messages and of the cursor.

[`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_webhook) runs the receiver (with uvicorn, the `server` extra) on
127.0.0.1:8082 unless `webhook_allow_remote` is set; put your HTTPS reverse proxy in
front, and point a repository or organization webhook (content type
`application/json`, the “Discussion comments” event) at it.

### Module Attributes

| [`EVENTS`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.EVENTS)       | The events the receiver keeps; any other signed event is acknowledged and dropped.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`WEBHOOK_KIND`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.WEBHOOK_KIND) | The data-root folder the receiver stores deliveries in.                              |

### Functions

| [`mk_webhook_app`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.mk_webhook_app)(\*, secret[, deliveries, ...])      | The receiver as an ASGI app: GitHub POSTs signed deliveries, the app stores the `events` ones in `deliveries`.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`serve_main`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_main)([argv])                                 | `correspond-github-webhook`: run the webhook receiver ([`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_webhook)).  |
| [`serve_webhook`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_webhook)(\*[, host, port, allow_remote, ...]) | Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.                                             |
| [`webhook_app_from_env`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.webhook_app_from_env)()                             | [`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.mk_webhook_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.   |
| [`webhook_store`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.webhook_store)()                                    | Where the receiver keeps deliveries: the `github` `webhook_store` setting's `module:attr`, else files under the data root. |

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.EVENTS *= ('discussion_comment',)*

The events the receiver keeps; any other signed event is acknowledged and dropped.

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.WEBHOOK_KIND *= 'github-webhook'*

The data-root folder the receiver stores deliveries in.

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.mk_webhook_app(\*, secret, deliveries=None, events=('discussion_comment', ), max_body_bytes=1000000, clock=<built-in function time_ns>, prune_every_ns=3600000000000)

The receiver as an ASGI app: GitHub POSTs signed deliveries, the app stores the `events` ones in `deliveries`.

A request whose `X-Hub-Signature-256` is not the HMAC of its body under `secret` is
refused (401) and nothing is read from it: the signature is the only gate, since behind
a reverse proxy every connection comes from this machine. A signed `ping` (sent when
the webhook is created) and any event not in `events` get 202 and are not stored. A
kept delivery is stored under `<delivery id>.json` as `{event, action,
repository, discussion, comment, received_ns}`: no comment text. Keyed by
GitHub’s delivery id, a replayed request (GitHub signatures carry no timestamp)
overwrites its first copy instead of growing the store. `deliveries`
defaults to files under the data root (`github-webhook/`).

The receiver also deletes deliveries older than `WEBHOOK_RETENTION` itself
(`prune_deliveries()`), on a write, at most once per `prune_every_ns`, so the
store stays bounded in time even with no `delivery = webhook` listen to prune it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_main(argv=None)

`correspond-github-webhook`: run the webhook receiver ([`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_webhook)).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.serve_webhook(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8082, allow_remote=None, app=None, run=None)

Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.

`allow_remote` defaults to the `github` `webhook_allow_remote` setting. Put your
HTTPS reverse proxy in front.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.webhook_app_from_env()

[`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#correspond.channels.github_webhook.mk_webhook_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.github_webhook.webhook_store()

Where the receiver keeps deliveries: the `github` `webhook_store` setting’s `module:attr`, else files under the data root.

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.html.md

# correspond.channels

The built-in channel adapters, one module each.

The registry imports a module only when its channel is first used, so an adapter’s
dependencies (none, for the v0.1 adapters) are never paid for by code that does not use
that channel.

### Modules

| [`apprise`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.apprise.html.md#module-correspond.channels.apprise)               | Apprise: send-only notifications to the long tail of services (about 155), each named by an alias.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`discord`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.discord.html.md#module-correspond.channels.discord)               | Discord: a bot reading and posting in channels over REST, through discorddol.                                  |
| [`gdrive`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.gdrive.html.md#module-correspond.channels.gdrive)                 | Google Drive: a shared folder, read only, where files that a conversation announces arrive.                    |
| [`github`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github.html.md#module-correspond.channels.github)                 | GitHub: issues, pull request conversations and discussions, through the `gh` CLI.                              |
| [`github_webhook`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.github_webhook.html.md#module-correspond.channels.github_webhook) | GitHub webhook receiver: `discussion_comment` deliveries, so listen sees every discussion reply.               |
| [`macos`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.macos.html.md#module-correspond.channels.macos)                   | macOS Notification Centre: a banner on this Mac (send only).                                                   |
| [`mail`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md#module-correspond.channels.mail)                     | Email: IMAP to read and listen, SMTP to send, with the standard library.                                       |
| [`ntfy`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.ntfy.html.md#module-correspond.channels.ntfy)                     | ntfy: push notifications to a phone or a desktop through an ntfy server (send only).                           |
| [`signal`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.signal.html.md#module-correspond.channels.signal)                 | Signal through `signal-cli-rest-api` (JSON-RPC mode): listen, read what was logged, send.                      |
| [`slack`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#module-correspond.channels.slack)                   | Slack: drafts in Slack's own formatting; reading, polling and posting with a token; posting through a webhook. |
| [`slack_events`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#module-correspond.channels.slack_events)     | Slack Events API receiver: Slack pushes a channel's messages, edits and deletions, so listen need not poll.    |
| [`telegram`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#module-correspond.channels.telegram)             | Telegram: a bot over the Bot API, with the standard library.                                                   |
| [`webinbox`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#module-correspond.channels.webinbox)             | The web inbox: a small ASGI collector web pages post reports to, and the channel that reads them.              |


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.macos.html.md

# correspond.channels.macos

macOS Notification Centre: a banner on this Mac (send only).

Reference: `macos:` (this machine; it takes no id). A send uses `terminal-notifier` when
it is installed, because it keeps bodies with quotes intact, and `osascript` otherwise.
Either way the text travels as program arguments, never inside a script, so nothing in a
message can be run.

```pycon

'macos:'
```

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md

# correspond.channels.mail

Email: IMAP to read and listen, SMTP to send, with the standard library.

### References

- `email:`: the whole folder (`INBOX` unless configured), which is what `listen` watches.
- `email:<address>`: the correspondence with one address: its messages in the folder,
  and sends to it.
- `?folder=<name>` after either picks the folder for this reference alone, so one process
  reads several (Gmail serves labels as folders: `email:?folder=Newsletters/AI`).
  `?from=<sender>,<sender>` on `email:` keeps the messages from any of several senders,
  each an address or a whole domain (`@example.org`). Both together:
  `email:?folder=News&from=ada@example.org,@example.net`. A value is percent-encoded
  where it has a space, `&`, `?` or `%` (`email:?folder=%5BGmail%5D/All%20Mail`), and
  so is an address with one of those. A folder may be named as written (`Énergie`) or as
  the server lists it in modified UTF-7 (`&AMk-nergie`); both are one reference. On a
  command line, quote a reference with `?` or `&`: `correspond read 'email:?folder=News'`.
- `?gmail=<search>` adds Gmail’s own search syntax (`X-GM-RAW`) on a server that
  advertises `X-GM-EXT-1`, and is refused elsewhere:
  `email:?gmail=category:promotions+newer_than:7d`. As in Gmail’s own addresses, `+`
  is a space (a plus sign is `%2B`). It narrows the other keys; it replaces none of them,
  so `?from=` still checks each From exactly. Listening delivers a message only if it
  matches when the listen first passes it: a search whose answer changes later
  (`is:starred`, a label added afterwards, `is:unread`) misses the mail that comes to
  match after newer mail has moved the cursor on.

A message’s conversation is the correspondence with its sender (`email:<address>`), in
whichever folder it was read; `native["folder"]` says which.

Message ids are `Message-ID` headers, angle brackets included. A draft’s `reply_to` is
one, and the send carries `In-Reply-To` and `References`. Reading never marks a message
seen.

Authenticity is `claimed` unless the **topmost** `Authentication-Results` header was
added by a server you trust (`trusted_authserv_ids`) and records `dmarc=pass` for the
From domain: then it is `domain`. Only the topmost header counts, even when the trusted
server added several: a lower one carrying the same authserv-id may have been written by the
sender (not every server strips those), so a result recorded lower down fails safe as
`claimed`.

```pycon
>>> Email().parse_ref("Ada@Example.org").encoded
'email:ada@example.org'
>>> Email().parse_ref("?from=@Example.NET,ada@example.org&folder=News/AI").encoded
'email:?folder=News/AI&from=@example.net,ada@example.org'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`LIST_LOCAL_PARTS`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md#correspond.channels.mail.LIST_LOCAL_PARTS)   | Words that, as a part of an address's local part (`dev-team@`), mark it as a possible mailing list.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`authenticity`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md#correspond.channels.mail.authenticity)(message, trusted_authserv_ids)   | `domain` only when the topmost Authentication-Results comes from a trusted server and DMARC passed for the From domain.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Email`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md#correspond.channels.mail.Email)(\*[, imap, smtp, run])   | A mailbox over IMAP and SMTP.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|

### *class* correspond.channels.mail.Email(\*, imap=None, smtp=None, run=<function run>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A mailbox over IMAP and SMTP.

#### audience(ref, , draft=None)

Who reads an email: its address plus the draft’s `cc` and `bcc`, asked of nothing but the config.

Scope `named`, never `complete`: any address may be an alias, a shared mailbox or
an auto-forward, which nothing here can see. A recipient whose domain is not in
`own_domains` makes it `external`; a list-shaped address (under `lists` in the
config, or a local part naming a group, see [`LIST_LOCAL_PARTS`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.mail.html.md#correspond.channels.mail.LIST_LOCAL_PARTS)) adds a class
and `list_expansion`, and, when every address is in an own domain, leaves
`external` unknown, since a list can have outside members. A Bcc address is a
class of its own, so moving it to Cc changes the hash. Every email is pushed to its
recipients, can be forwarded, and cannot be recalled.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

Read and listen to a folder per reference; send with threading headers.

#### parse_ref(id)

`""` for the folder, or an address; either may add `?folder=` (and the folder `?from=`).

* **Return type:**
  [`ConversationRef`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.ConversationRef)

#### poll(ref, , cursor=None, limit=None)

New messages since `cursor` (`<uidvalidity>:<uid>`); a first poll, or a changed UIDVALIDITY, looks back a day.

#### prepare(ref, draft)

The draft as it will go out: `notify` addresses checked and put in Cc (out of Bcc). Pure.

* **Return type:**
  [`Draft`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Draft)

#### read(ref, , since=None, limit=None)

Messages in the reference’s folder (from its address or senders, if it names any), oldest first; never marked seen.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message)]

#### send(ref, draft, , dry_run=False)

Send to `ref`’s address, with `In-Reply-To` and `References` when replying; `cc` in a header, `bcc` only on the envelope.

A `draft.notify` address that is neither the To address nor already in Cc is
added to Cc (and so leaves Bcc, which would hide it); the plan lists it under
`cc_added`.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### upload(ref, name, data, , media_type='application/octet-stream', dry_run=False)

Email a file to `ref`’s address: a message with the file attached and its name as the subject.

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.ntfy.html.md

# correspond.channels.ntfy

ntfy: push notifications to a phone or a desktop through an ntfy server (send only).

### References

`ntfy:<topic>`, or `ntfy:` for the default topic, which is resolved in this
order: `$NTFY_TOPIC`; the macOS Keychain (service `topic_keychain_service` in the
`[ntfy]` config table, default `correspond-ntfy-topic`); an ssh host named by
`topic_remote`, asked for the `NTFY_TOPIC=...` line of `topic_remote_file`. A dry run
reads only the environment and the config file (no Keychain, no remote host: those are looked
up when sending), and a plan shows a topic masked.

A topic is a bearer secret: anyone who knows an unauthenticated one can publish to it and
read it. Prefer `ntfy:` to writing a topic into a reference that ends up in logs.

```pycon
>>> Ntfy().parse_ref("").kind
'topic'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`PRIORITY`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.ntfy.html.md#correspond.channels.ntfy.PRIORITY)   | Draft priorities as ntfy's 1-5 scale.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|

Nothing is asked of the server. Its cache keeps each message for subscribers who

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.signal.html.md

# correspond.channels.signal

Signal through `signal-cli-rest-api` (JSON-RPC mode): listen, read what was logged, send.

### References

`signal:` (the linked account’s receive stream, for `listen`),
`signal:+<number>` (a person, by international phone number or Signal uuid) and
`signal:group.<id>` (a group, by the REST API’s group id).

Signal has no bot API. `signal-cli` runs as a *linked device* (or a registered number) of
an account you control, and the REST wrapper exposes it: `POST /v2/send` to send,
`GET /v1/receive/<number>` (a WebSocket in JSON-RPC mode) to receive. The WebSocket client
is the optional `websocket-client` (extra `signal`); tests and other transports pass
`ws=`.

Three facts shape the adapter:

- There is no history before linking: `read` returns only what `listen` and `send`
  logged on this machine (`history_depth = since_link`).
- `signal-cli` releases older than about three months stop working against Signal’s
  servers, so a silent channel may just be an old release (`requirements signal` says so).
- Whether to trust a changed safety number is an authenticity policy of the server
  (`--trust-new-identities`). `listen` compares the account’s known identities on every
  poll and reports a changed safety number as an `identity.changed` event.

```pycon
>>> Signal().parse_ref("group.ZXhhbXBsZQ==").kind
'group'
```

### Functions

| [`requirements_problems`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.signal.html.md#correspond.channels.signal.requirements_problems)()            | What stops Signal working from this configuration; the signal-cli age caveat is a note, not a problem.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`websocket_frames`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.signal.html.md#correspond.channels.signal.websocket_frames)(url, \*, timeout) | Text frames of the WebSocket at `url` until it has been quiet for `timeout` seconds (the default `ws=`). |

| [`Signal`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.signal.html.md#correspond.channels.signal.Signal)(\*[, http, ws, log])   | A Signal account linked to a `signal-cli-rest-api` server.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md

# correspond.channels.slack

Slack: drafts in Slack’s own formatting; reading, polling and posting with a token; posting through a webhook.

Reference: `slack:<channel>`, a Slack channel by its name (`#` optional, lower-cased;
1-80 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` and `_`) or by its id (`C024BE91L`, kept as Slack
writes it). A post goes through the channel’s **incoming webhook**, which Slack ties to one
channel when it is created: `$CORRESPOND_SLACK_WEBHOOK_<CHANNEL>` (upper case, `-` as
`_` and `_` as `__`, so no two channels share a variable), else on macOS the Keychain
item `correspond-slack-webhook-<channel>`. The webhook URL is a credential: it never
appears in a reference, a plan or an error.

Three uses, one channel, each needing a little more set up:

- **A draft the operator sends.** `send(..., dry_run=True)` needs nothing configured: the
  plan holds the text rendered as Slack `mrkdwn` ([`to_mrkdwn()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.to_mrkdwn)), its length against
  Slack’s limit, and says nothing was sent. That is the whole interaction when an agent
  writes the reply and a person pastes it, including on a workspace where no app will
  ever be installed.
- **A post through a webhook.** With the channel’s webhook, `send` posts the same text
  there, as the app that owns the webhook. A webhook cannot reply in a thread.
- **The Web API, with a token** (`CORRESPOND_SLACK_TOKEN`: a bot token `xoxb-` acts as
  the app, a user token `xoxp-` as the person). `read` returns a channel’s latest
  top-level messages (`conversations.history`), `listen` polls for newer ones (the
  cursor is a message `ts`), and `send` posts with `chat.postMessage`, replying in a
  thread when `reply_to` is a message’s `ts`. A channel given by name is looked up
  once with `conversations.list`. Install the app in your own workspace: Slack limits a
  commercially distributed app outside its Marketplace to one history request a minute.
  [`Slack.verify()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.Slack.verify) checks a request Slack sends (`X-Slack-Signature`, with the
  > signing secret), graded `crypto`.

Slack’s `mrkdwn` is not Markdown: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `<url|text>`
links, no headings, no tables, and `&`, `<` and `>` escaped. [`to_mrkdwn()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.to_mrkdwn)
converts the common Markdown into it, so a draft written as GitHub Markdown does not paste
as literal asterisks and pipes. Because every `<` in the text is escaped, a draft cannot
carry a Slack mention (`<!channel>`, `<@U...>`) that would notify people.

Messages read are `platform`: Slack authenticated the account, and correspond fetched
them itself. Neither the token nor a webhook URL appears in a plan or an error.

```pycon
>>> to_mrkdwn("**Fixed** in [#12](https://example.org/12) & shipped")
'*Fixed* in <https://example.org/12|#12> &amp; shipped'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`MAX_TEXT_CHARS`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.MAX_TEXT_CHARS)   | Slack truncates a message's text past this many characters.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`to_mrkdwn`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.to_mrkdwn)(markdown)   | Common Markdown as Slack `mrkdwn`: bold, italic, strike, links, headings, lists, code, quotes, tables as code.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`webhook_env`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.webhook_env)(name)     | The environment variable holding one name's webhook URL.                                                         |

#### audience(ref, , draft=None)

The channel’s members, never listed; a shared channel reaches other workspaces.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

post; with nothing: a draft.

* **Type:**
  With a token
* **Type:**
  read, poll, post and reply in threads; with a webhook

#### *property* events *: [MutableMapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*

What the Events API receiver stored (read when `delivery` is `events`).

#### parse_ref(id)

A channel’s id as Slack writes it, or its name, `#` optional, lower-cased; `/<thread ts>` after it names one thread.

* **Return type:**
  [`ConversationRef`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.ConversationRef)

#### poll(ref, , cursor=None, limit=None)

Top-level messages newer than `cursor`, oldest first; a first poll looks back a day.

Slack returns history newest first, so a poll walks forward through time windows
(`oldest` = the cursor’s `ts`, `latest` = it plus a width, both included):
each window comes back whole and is delivered before the next, and the cursor moves
to its end, never past Slack’s own clock (its `Date`) less a minute. A window
holding a full page is narrowed, from that page’s own spread, and asked again; an
empty one widens the next. The cursor is `<ts>/<width>`, so a poll that only
narrowed or widened still moves forward, and a plain `ts` (an older cursor) is
read too. A poll stops after `MAX_REQUESTS_PER_POLL` requests, at `limit`
events, or at a rate limit, keeping what it delivered: the next resumes there.

#### read(ref, , since=None, limit=None)

The channel’s latest top-level messages (`limit`, else 50), oldest first; for a thread, its parent and replies.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message)]

#### send(ref, draft, , dry_run=False)

Render `draft` as mrkdwn, then post it with the token (`chat.postMessage`), else through the channel’s webhook.

`draft.reply_to` (a message’s `ts`) posts in that thread with a token; through a
webhook, which cannot thread, it renders in a dry run for the operator to paste.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### verify(headers, body)

`crypto` when `X-Slack-Signature` matches the signing secret over a fresh timestamp, `forged` otherwise.

Raises [`MissingRequirement`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.MissingRequirement) when the signing secret is
unset (a configuration error, never a verdict on the request). Anything that is not
a well-formed signed request (headers that are not a mapping, a body that is not
bytes, a timestamp that is not a short run of digits) is graded `forged`, never
raised. Replay protection is the five-minute window only: act idempotently on an
event’s id.

* **Return type:**
  [`Authenticity`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Authenticity)

### correspond.channels.slack.to_mrkdwn(markdown)

Common Markdown as Slack `mrkdwn`: bold, italic, strike, links, headings, lists, code, quotes, tables as code.

Only `http`, `https` and `mailto` targets become links: a Markdown link to
`!channel` or `@U123` stays text, so no draft can notify a channel or a person.

```pycon
>>> to_mrkdwn("# Release\n- **new**: _faster_ export\n- ~~old~~ gone")
'*Release*\n• *new*: _faster_ export\n• ~old~ gone'
>>> to_mrkdwn("> quoted <b> & `a < b`")
'> quoted &lt;b&gt; &amp; `a &lt; b`'
>>> to_mrkdwn("[ping](!channel)")
'ping (!channel)'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### correspond.channels.slack.webhook_env(name)

The environment variable holding one name’s webhook URL.

```pycon
>>> webhook_env("team-alerts"), webhook_env("team_alerts")
('CORRESPOND_SLACK_WEBHOOK_TEAM_ALERTS', 'CORRESPOND_SLACK_WEBHOOK_TEAM__ALERTS')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md

# correspond.channels.slack_events

Slack Events API receiver: Slack pushes a channel’s messages, edits and deletions, so listen need not poll.

[`mk_events_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.mk_events_app) is the receiver, an ASGI app that checks every request with
[`verify()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.Slack.verify) (`X-Slack-Signature` under the signing
secret, over a timestamp at most five minutes old: nothing unverified is read), answers
Slack’s `url_verification` challenge, and keeps the `message` events under the data
root (`slack-events/`). With `delivery = "events"` in the `slack` config, `listen`
reads what the receiver stored instead of polling `conversations.history`, and reports
edits (`message.updated`) and deletions (`message.deleted`) too.

[`serve_events()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_events) runs the receiver (with uvicorn, the `server` extra) on
127.0.0.1:8083 unless `webhook_allow_remote` is set; put your HTTPS reverse proxy in
front, and give its URL as the app’s Event Subscriptions Request URL, subscribed to the
bot events `message.channels` (and `message.groups` for private channels).

### Functions

| [`events_app_from_env`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.events_app_from_env)()                             | [`mk_events_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.mk_events_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`events_store`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.events_store)()                                    | Where the receiver keeps events: the `slack` `webhook_store` setting's `module:attr`, else files under the data root.     |
| [`mk_events_app`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.mk_events_app)(\*[, verify, events, ...])          | The receiver as an ASGI app: Slack POSTs signed requests, the app stores the `message` events in `events`.                |
| [`prune_events`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.prune_events)(events, \*, now_ns[, retention_ns])  | Delete the stored events that arrived more than `retention_ns` before `now_ns`; return how many.                          |
| [`serve_events`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_events)(\*[, host, port, allow_remote, ...]) | Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.                                            |
| [`serve_main`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_main)([argv])                                | `correspond-slack-events`: run the Events API receiver ([`serve_events()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_events)). |

### correspond.channels.slack_events.events_app_from_env()

[`mk_events_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.mk_events_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.

The signing secret is required here, so a receiver without one refuses to start
rather than refusing every request.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.slack_events.events_store()

Where the receiver keeps events: the `slack` `webhook_store` setting’s `module:attr`, else files under the data root.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### correspond.channels.slack_events.mk_events_app(\*, verify=None, events=None, max_body_bytes=1000000, clock=<built-in function time_ns>, prune_every_ns=3600000000000)

The receiver as an ASGI app: Slack POSTs signed requests, the app stores the `message` events in `events`.

`verify` grades a request from its headers and raw body; only `crypto` passes,
anything else gets 401 and nothing is read from it. It defaults to
[`Slack.verify`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack.html.md#correspond.channels.slack.Slack.verify) (the signing secret,
five-minute window). A verified `url_verification` gets its challenge back; any
other verified request that is not a `message` event is acknowledged (200) and
dropped. A kept event is stored under `<arrival ns>-<event id>.json` as
`{event_id, team_id, channel, event, received_ns}`; a retry Slack sends for an event
already stored (a retry, `X-Slack-Retry-Num`, or a replay within the signature’s
window) is acknowledged and not stored twice.
`events` defaults to files under the data root (`slack-events/`).

The receiver deletes events older than the retention itself ([`prune_events()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.prune_events)),
on a write, at most once per `prune_every_ns`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.slack_events.prune_events(events, , now_ns, retention_ns=604800000000000)

Delete the stored events that arrived more than `retention_ns` before `now_ns`; return how many.

Only keys the receiver writes are considered: anything else in the store is left alone.

```pycon
>>> store = {"00000000000000000001-Ev1.json": {}, "00000000000000000009-Ev2.json": {}, "x": 0}
>>> prune_events(store, now_ns=10, retention_ns=5)
1
>>> sorted(store)
['00000000000000000009-Ev2.json', 'x']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_events(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8083, allow_remote=None, app=None, run=None)

Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.

`allow_remote` defaults to the `slack` `webhook_allow_remote` setting. Put your
HTTPS reverse proxy in front.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_main(argv=None)

`correspond-slack-events`: run the Events API receiver ([`serve_events()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.slack_events.html.md#correspond.channels.slack_events.serve_events)).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md

# correspond.channels.telegram

Telegram: a bot over the Bot API, with the standard library.

### References

`telegram:` (the bot’s whole update stream, for listening),
`telegram:<chat id>` (a private chat, a group or a channel; `telegram:@name` for a
public channel), `telegram:<chat id>/<topic id>` (a forum topic).

Bots have no history API, and Telegram keeps undelivered updates for at most 24 hours, so
`poll` writes every update it receives to a local log under the data root
(`telegram/`) and `read` reads that log (a `telegram:@name` reference is first resolved
with `getChat`, over the network). `getUpdates` confirms updates for every chat
at once, which is why listening is account-wide: narrow to one chat when routing.

Senders are `platform`: Telegram authenticated the account, and correspond pulled the
update from the Bot API itself. The bot token never appears in an error or a plan.

**Webhook delivery**, for a server: [`Telegram.set_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram.set_webhook) asks Telegram to POST
every update, one at a time, to an HTTPS address, carrying the configured
`webhook_secret` in the `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header.
[`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.mk_webhook_app) is the receiver, an ASGI app that stores each update carrying that
secret under the data root (`telegram-webhook/`), in the order it arrives; the secret is
the gate, and nothing without it is stored. [`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.serve_webhook) runs it (with uvicorn,
the `server` extra) on `127.0.0.1` behind your own HTTPS reverse proxy, and refuses
any other address unless `webhook_allow_remote` is set. With `delivery = "webhook"` in
the config, `listen` reads what the receiver stored instead of calling `getUpdates`:
Telegram serves one or the other, never both, so while a webhook is set `getUpdates` is
refused (409), and [`Telegram.delete_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram.delete_webhook) returns the bot to polling.
[`Telegram.verify()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram.verify) grades one delivery by the same header.

```pycon
>>> Telegram().parse_ref("-4001/7").parent.encoded
'telegram:-4001'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`SECRET_HEADER`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.SECRET_HEADER)   | The header Telegram puts the webhook's secret token in.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`mk_webhook_app`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.mk_webhook_app)(\*, secret[, updates, ...])         | The webhook receiver as an ASGI app: Telegram POSTs updates, the app stores them in `updates`.                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`serve_main`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.serve_main)([argv])                                 | `correspond-telegram-webhook`: run the webhook receiver ([`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.serve_webhook)). |
| [`serve_webhook`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.serve_webhook)(\*[, host, port, allow_remote, ...]) | Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.                                              |
| [`webhook_app_from_env`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.webhook_app_from_env)()                             | [`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.mk_webhook_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.    |
| [`webhook_store`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.webhook_store)()                                    | Where the receiver keeps updates: the `webhook_store` setting's `module:attr`, else files under the data root.              |

### Classes

### correspond.channels.telegram.SECRET_HEADER *= 'x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token'*

### *class* correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram(\*, http=<function urllib_http>, log=None, updates=None, run=<function run>, clock=<built-in function time_ns>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A Telegram bot: listen, read the local log, send, edit, react.

#### audience(ref, , draft=None)

Who reads a chat, from `getChat`; a topic has its chat’s readers.

- A private chat: `named`, the other account (by its id only, so a rename keeps
  the hash) as its reader.
- A chat with a public username: `public`.
- A group or supergroup without one: `group`; a channel without one: `group`
  of its subscribers. Members are never listed.
- A linked chat (a channel’s discussion group, or the channel a group discusses)
  is read too: posts are copied into it. A public linked chat makes the audience
  public; one that cannot be read makes it unknown.

Joiners read the history unless `getChat` says the history is hidden from them.
Forwarding widens every chat unless its content is protected. A failed `getChat`
raises, so the audience resolves to public, defaulted.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* capabilities *: [Capabilities](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Capabilities)*

A bot’s view of Telegram.

#### delete_webhook(, drop_pending_updates=False, dry_run=False)

Stop webhook delivery, so `getUpdates` works again; pending updates are kept unless `drop_pending_updates`.

* **Return type:**
  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Message`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Message)]

`sendMessage`, the title (if any) prepended; `draft.notify` usernames the text does not @mention yet are mentioned on a closing `cc` line.

#### set_webhook(url, , dry_run=False)

Have Telegram POST this bot’s updates to `url` (HTTPS), with the configured `webhook_secret`.

`getUpdates` stops working until [`delete_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram.delete_webhook); set `delivery =
"webhook"` so `listen` reads what the receiver stores. The plan reads the
webhook back with `getWebhookInfo`. A dry run calls nothing and reads no secret.

  [`SendResult`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.SendResult)

#### *property* updates *: [MutableMapping](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*

What the webhook receiver stored, keyed by zero-padded update id (`listen` reads it when `delivery` is `webhook`).

#### upload(ref, name, data, , media_type='application/octet-stream', dry_run=False, native=None)

Send a file: `sendPhoto` for an inline image (`PHOTO_TYPES`, 10 MB), else `sendDocument` (50 MB).

A photo Telegram refuses (too large in pixels, too narrow, not really an image) is
sent again as a document, which takes any file; the plan says so (`photo_refused`).
`native={"as_document": True}` sends an image as a document: the file as it is,
not recompressed.

`platform` when the delivery carries the configured `webhook_secret`, `forged` otherwise.

The secret token proves Telegram sent the request (only Telegram and this machine
know it); it signs nothing, so the grade is Telegram’s own, not `crypto`.

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### correspond.channels.telegram.mk_webhook_app(\*, secret, updates=None, max_body_bytes=1000000, clock=<built-in function time_ns>)

The webhook receiver as an ASGI app: Telegram POSTs updates, the app stores them in `updates`.

A request without `secret` in `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` is refused (401)
and nothing is stored: the secret is the only gate, since behind a reverse proxy every
connection comes from this machine. Each update is stored under
`<arrival time in ns>-<update id>.json`, so `listen` takes them in the order they
came, whatever their ids (Telegram restarts them at random after a week without
updates). One receiver process per bot keeps that order: [`Telegram.set_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.Telegram.set_webhook)
asks Telegram for one connection at a time. `updates` defaults to files under the
data root (`telegram-webhook/`), which `listen` reads when `delivery` is
`webhook`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.telegram.serve_main(argv=None)

`correspond-telegram-webhook`: run the webhook receiver ([`serve_webhook()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.serve_webhook)).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channels.telegram.serve_webhook(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8081, allow_remote=None, app=None, run=None)

Run the receiver (with uvicorn) on `host`, this machine unless `allow_remote`.

`allow_remote` defaults to the `webhook_allow_remote` setting. Put your HTTPS
reverse proxy in front: Telegram reaches only public HTTPS addresses. Proxy headers are
ignored, since the receiver needs no client address, and one worker keeps the order.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### correspond.channels.telegram.webhook_app_from_env()

[`mk_webhook_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.telegram.html.md#correspond.channels.telegram.mk_webhook_app) configured from the settings, for `uvicorn --factory`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Awaitable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Awaitable)[[`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### correspond.channels.telegram.webhook_store()

Where the receiver keeps updates: the `webhook_store` setting’s `module:attr`, else files under the data root.

The reference names a `MutableMapping`, or a callable returning one, whose values are
JSON-ready dicts (an update as Telegram sent it): a bytes store, such as a plain
`s3dol` one, needs a JSON codec around it. The receiver and `listen` read the same
setting, so they meet in the same store.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]


# _autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md

# correspond.channels.webinbox

The web inbox: a small ASGI collector web pages post reports to, and the channel that reads them.

**The collector** ([`mk_app()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#correspond.channels.webinbox.mk_app); or `uvicorn --factory correspond.channels.webinbox:app_from_env`)
accepts `POST /<site>/reports` with a JSON body:

```default
{"text": "The export drops the last row.",
 "name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.org",
 "page": "https://app.example.org/export",
 "context": {"viewport": "1280x800"},
 "identity": {"user": "u-42", "name": "Ada", "email": null, "issued_at": 1757592000, "sig": "<hex>"},
 "attachments": [{"name": "screen.png", "media_type": "image/png", "data": "<base64>"}]}
```

Only `text` is required.

- **Identity.** Without `identity` a report is `claimed` (`name` and `email` are
  whatever was typed). With one, the host application’s *server* has signed its logged-in
  user with the site’s secret ([`sign_identity()`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#correspond.channels.webinbox.sign_identity)); a valid, fresh signature makes the
  report `bound`. An invalid or expired signature is refused with 401 and nothing is
  stored.
- **Origins.** A browser’s `Origin` must be on the site’s allowlist (403 otherwise); a
  request without one is refused unless the site allows server-to-server posts. CORS
  preflight is answered for allowed origins only. An origin check stops other pages from
  posting through a visitor’s browser; it authenticates no one.
- **Limits.** A per-client token bucket (429 with `Retry-After`), the body size (413),
  caps on text, context and attachments, and a media-type allowlist.
- **Storage.** A report is JSON in `store` under `<site>/<sortable id>.json`;
  attachments are bytes in `blobs` under their SHA-256, referenced and never inlined.

The app binds nothing: run it on localhost behind your own server, and tell it how many
reverse proxies stand in front (`trusted_proxies`) so the rate limit applies per visitor
rather than to the proxy. The limiter lives in memory, per process. Each site has its own
secret, so a server that can sign for one site cannot sign for another.

**The channel** ([`WebInbox`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#correspond.channels.webinbox.WebInbox)): `webinbox:<site>` reads and listens to what the
collector stored. It has no writer: a reply to a reporter goes out on another channel.

The identity payload is plain lines, so any server language can sign it:

```pycon
>>> identity_payload("example-site", "u-42", 1757592000, name="Ada")
b'v1\nexample-site\n1757592000\nu-42\nAda\n'
```

| [`mk_app`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#correspond.channels.webinbox.mk_app)(sites, \*[, store, blobs, ...])             | The collector as an ASGI app, storing reports in `store` and attachments in `blobs` (files under the data root by default).                  |
| [`requirements_problems`](_autosummary/correspond.channels.webinbox.html.md#correspond.channels.webinbox.requirements_problems)()                            | What would stop the collector starting from this configuration; nothing when no site is configured, since reading stored reports needs none. |

# _autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md

# correspond.errors

What correspond raises, and the vocabulary a failed write reports.

Two families, on purpose:

- **Mistakes a caller fixes in code or configuration raise**: an unknown channel
  ([`UnknownChannel`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.UnknownChannel)), a malformed conversation reference ([`InvalidRef`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.InvalidRef)), an
  operation the channel does not have ([`NotSupported`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.NotSupported)). A retry changes nothing.
- **Failures of the platform or of the message** are [`ChannelError`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.ChannelError) inside an
  adapter, carrying an `kind` from [`ERROR_KINDS`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.ERROR_KINDS), `retryable` and
  `retry_after`. Reads let them propagate; the write verbs turn them into a
  `SendResult` with `ok=False`, so a notifier never crashes its caller.

A third family stops a write before it leaves: the `before_send` check (see
[`correspond.outbound`](_autosummary/correspond.outbound.html.md#module-correspond.outbound)) raises [`Refused`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.Refused) or [`NeedsApproval`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.NeedsApproval), and the write
verbs report it as a `SendResult` whose `error_kind` is one of [`CHECK_KINDS`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.CHECK_KINDS).

```pycon
>>> str(NotSupported("react", "ntfy"))
'ntfy does not support react'
>>> error = ChannelError("slow down", kind="rate_limited", retryable=True, retry_after=30)
>>> error.kind, error.retryable, error.retry_after
('rate_limited', True, 30.0)
>>> held = NeedsApproval("public audience")
>>> held.error_kind, held.reason
('needs_approval', 'public audience')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`ERROR_KINDS`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.ERROR_KINDS)   | Why a platform call failed, for a caller deciding whether to retry, fix the draft, or ask a human.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CHECK_KINDS`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.CHECK_KINDS)   | Why the `before_send` check stopped a write.                                                         |

### Exceptions

| [`BeforeSendFailed`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.BeforeSendFailed)(reason, \*\*details)             | The `before_send` check raised something else, or returned a value, so nothing is sent.      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`BeforeSendUnavailable`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.BeforeSendUnavailable)(reason, \*\*details)        | The configured `before_send` check could not be loaded, so nothing is sent.                  |
| [`ChannelError`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.ChannelError)(message, \*, kind[, retryable, ...]) | A platform call that failed, classified so the caller can decide what to do.                 |
| [`CorrespondError`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.CorrespondError)                                   | An expected failure, with a message meant for the person or agent that asked.                |
| [`InvalidRef`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.InvalidRef)                                        | A conversation reference that does not parse, or that its channel rejects.                   |
| [`MissingRequirement`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.MissingRequirement)(channel, missing, \*, fix)     | Something the channel needs is not here: a credential, a binary, an extra, an OS.            |
| [`NeedsApproval`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.NeedsApproval)(reason, \*\*details)                | Draft to operator: the write waits for the operator's approval.                              |
| [`NotSupported`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.NotSupported)(operation, channel, \*[, ...])       | The channel does not have this operation (or this feature of it).                            |
| [`Refused`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.Refused)(reason, \*\*details)                      | Block: this draft does not go to this conversation as written.                               |
| [`Stopped`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.Stopped)(reason, \*\*details)                      | A write the `before_send` check did not let leave: `error_kind` says how, `reason` says why. |
| [`UnknownChannel`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.UnknownChannel)(channel, \*[, known, hint])        | A channel name that no registered adapter answers to.                                        |

# _autosummary/correspond.html.md

# correspond

correspond: a channel facade for AI agents.

Read, listen, write and identify the sender over GitHub, email, push notifications,
Telegram and a web inbox, through one model and one set of verbs:

```default
>>> import correspond
>>> messages = correspond.read("github:octocat/hello-world#1")
>>> messages[0].author.handle, messages[0].authenticity.grade.value
('octocat', 'platform')
>>> correspond.send("ntfy:", "backup finished", dry_run=True).plan
```

A conversation reference is `<channel>:<id>`. Each channel implements the operations it
can (`read`, `listen`, `send`, `edit`, `react`, `upload`, `verify`,
`audience`, `label`, `unlabel`, `close`, `reopen`); asking for one it lacks raises [`NotSupported`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.NotSupported), and
[`capabilities()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.capabilities) says so in advance. [`audience()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.audience) is the exception: it never
refuses, because an audience nobody can compute is public.
correspond knows no people: a message’s `author` is what the platform attests, and its
`authenticity` is how sure the channel is.

The command line (`correspond read github:octocat/hello-world#1`) and the MCP server use
the same verbs, through [`correspond.tools`](_autosummary/correspond.tools.html.md#module-correspond.tools).

### Functions

| [`audience`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.audience)(ref[, draft, registry])                   | Who can read a conversation, asked of its channel now.                                                                                                                            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`capabilities`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.capabilities)(channel, \*[, registry])              | What a channel can do, graded, with its limits.                                                                                                                                   |
| [`channel_registry`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.channel_registry)()                                 | The process registry: built on first use, then shared.                                                                                                                            |
| [`check_binding`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.check_binding)(pattern, \*[, registry])             | What would make a binding never match, found when bindings are loaded instead of by messages quietly going unrouted.                                                              |
| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.check_requirements)(channel, \*[, registry, ...])   | What a channel needs and what is missing: the install command, binaries, platform, and every setting's source.                                                                    |
| [`close`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.close)(ref, \*[, reason, dry_run, registry, ...])   | Close a conversation (an issue or a discussion), with an optional `reason` in the channel's vocabulary; the `before_send` check sees the reason (or `close`) as the draft's text. |
| [`edit`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.edit)(ref, message_id, text, \*[, dry_run, ...])    | Replace the text of a message correspond's account wrote; the `before_send` check runs first, as for [`send()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.send).                     |
| [`get_channel`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.get_channel)(name, \*[, registry])                  | The adapter registered under `name`; [`UnknownChannel`](_autosummary/correspond.errors.html.md#correspond.errors.UnknownChannel) says what to do if there is none.           |

### *class* correspond.Audience(, ref, scope, readers=(), complete=False, classes=(), external=None, retractable=False, durability=(), widening=(), as_of=\_now(), evidence=(), defaulted=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Who can read a conversation, now and plausibly later, as far as its channel can tell.

`scope` is the widest class of reader it can reach. `readers` are the channel
identities known to read it, a lower bound unless `complete`; `classes` name, in
words, the readers that cannot be listed. `external` says whether readers outside
the operator’s own accounts exist (`None`: unknown). `durability` is what a send
leaves behind (`DURABILITY`), `widening` how the readership can grow
(`WIDENING`). `evidence` records the calls made and why anything was assumed;
`defaulted` is true when an unknown resolved to `public`, which it always does.

Set-valued fields (`readers`, `classes`, `durability`, `widening`) are stored
deduplicated and sorted, so the same audience compares and hashes alike whatever
order a platform listed it in. A durability or widening flag this version does not
know is kept, never dropped. A public audience is never complete, retractable or free
of external readers, and a defaulted one is always public.

```pycon
>>> a = Audience(ref="github:example/app#12", scope="public", classes=["watchers and participants receive the body by email"],
...              durability=["indexed", "archived_by_others", "copies_pushed", "edit_history_visible"], as_of="2026-09-15T12:00:00Z")
>>> a.in_words()
'world-readable; emailed to watchers and participants; archived by others; edits keep a visible history; not retractable'
>>> Audience.from_dict(a.to_dict()) == a
True
```

#### *classmethod* from_dict(data)

The inverse of [`to_dict()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.Audience.to_dict); unknown keys are ignored.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)

#### *property* hash *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The SHA-256, in hex, of the canonical JSON of [`to_dict()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.Audience.to_dict) without `AUDIENCE_UNHASHED`.

`data` is exactly what [`to_dict()`](_autosummary/correspond.html.md#correspond.Audience.to_dict) returns, derived `readers[].address`
included. Canonical JSON is `json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))`
(Python’s default ASCII escaping), encoded as UTF-8. Approvals bind to this value,
so the construction is a contract. A `to_dict` output can be hashed as it stands;
any other dict should go through `Audience.from_dict(d).hash`, which normalises.

#### in_words()

One line: the scope, the readers and reader classes, what a send leaves behind, whether it can be withdrawn.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### to_dict()

JSON-ready.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### *classmethod* unknown(ref, \*reasons)

The audience nobody could compute: public, incomplete, every durability and widening flag, not retractable, defaulted, with `reasons` as evidence.

* **Return type:**
  [`Audience`](_autosummary/correspond.model.html.md#correspond.model.Audience)
